results.name: near_vs_mid_distance_gradient
results.description: Yes rate for targets 1-3 away from the nearest example minus yes rate for targets 8-15 away (targets not in the set); observed < null means people's similarity gradient is flatter than the model's interval-driven gradient (model overpredicts yes for close neighbours relative to moderately distant ones).
results.code:
# name: near_vs_mid_distance_gradient
# description: Yes rate for targets 1-3 away from the nearest example minus yes rate for targets 8-15 away (targets not in the set); observed < null means people's similarity gradient is flatter than the model's interval-driven gradient (model overpredicts yes for close neighbours relative to moderately distant ones).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    near = (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 3)
    mid = (dist >= 8) & (dist <= 15)
    if near.sum() == 0 or mid.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[near].mean() - r[mid].mean())

results.name: single_example_generalization_rate
results.description: Yes rate on single-example sets for targets different from the example; observed > null means the model generalizes too narrowly from one example (too-strong size principle / too-narrow intervals), observed < null means it generalizes too broadly.
results.code:
# name: single_example_generalization_rate
# description: Yes rate on single-example sets for targets different from the example; observed > null means the model generalizes too narrowly from one example (too-strong size principle / too-narrow intervals), observed < null means it generalizes too broadly.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    single = ~s.str.contains(",").to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    first = pd.to_numeric(s.str.split(",").str[0]).to_numpy()
    m = single & (t != first)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[m].mean())

results.name: lag1_residual_autocorr
results.description: Within-participant correlation between consecutive responses after subtracting each participant's mean yes rate; observed > null means people show response perseveration/streakiness (sequential dependence) that the model, with independent trials, underproduces.
results.code:
# name: lag1_residual_autocorr
# description: Within-participant correlation between consecutive responses after subtracting each participant's mean yes rate; observed > null means people show response perseveration/streakiness (sequential dependence) that the model, with independent trials, underproduces.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    pid = (ti == 0).cumsum()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    res = r - pd.Series(r).groupby(pid).transform("mean").to_numpy()
    same = pid[1:] == pid[:-1]
    a, b = res[:-1][same], res[1:][same]
    if a.std() == 0 or b.std() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.corrcoef(a, b)[0, 1])

results.name: small_rule_member_contrast
results.description: For sets of 2+ examples all fitting a small rule (<=12 members: squares, cubes, powers of k, multiples of 8-12, ends-in-digit), yes rate for unshown targets in the smallest such rule minus yes rate for targets outside it; observed < null means the model's without-replacement size principle overcommits to small rules (people generalize less sharply along the rule), observed > null means people are even more rule-bound than the model.

results.name: participant_yes_rate_sd
results.description: SD across participants (participant = run of trials starting at trial_index 0) of the overall yes rate; observed > null means the model (one shared parameter set, no individual differences) underproduces between-person heterogeneity in yes-bias/generalization breadth.
results.code:
# name: participant_yes_rate_sd
# description: SD across participants (participant = run of trials starting at trial_index 0) of the overall yes rate; observed > null means the model (one shared parameter set, no individual differences) underproduces between-person heterogeneity in yes-bias/generalization breadth.
def test_statistic(df):
    pid = (df["trial_index"].to_numpy() == 0).cumsum()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    means = pd.Series(r).groupby(pid).mean()
    return float(means.std(ddof=0))

results.name: in_range_minus_out_range_multi
results.description: Among sets with 2+ examples and targets not in the set, yes rate for targets inside [min,max] of the examples minus yes rate for targets outside that span; observed < null means the model overweights the convex range (interval) hypothesis relative to people, observed > null means people respect the span more sharply than the model.
results.code:
# name: in_range_minus_out_range_multi
# description: Among sets with 2+ examples and targets not in the set, yes rate for targets inside [min,max] of the examples minus yes rate for targets outside that span; observed < null means the model overweights the convex range (interval) hypothesis relative to people, observed > null means people respect the span more sharply than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n = (~np.isnan(ex)).sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    lo, hi = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1), np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    inset = (ex == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    base = (n >= 2) & ~inset
    inside = base & (t >= lo) & (t <= hi)
    outside = base & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    if inside.sum() == 0 or outside.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[inside].mean() - r[outside].mean())

results.name: target_in_set_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate when the target is itself one of the shown examples; observed < null means the model overpredicts endorsement of shown examples (people say no to them more than posterior membership implies, e.g. a no-repeat belief or lapses), observed > null means the model's noise share makes it underpredict.

results.name: late_minus_early_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate in the second half of each session (trial_index >= 225) minus the first half; a nonzero observed value beyond the null means people drift in yes-bias over the session (fatigue/learning), which the stationary model does not produce.
